steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Whisk together the flour, cocoa powder, and baking soda.

Beat the butter, white sugar, and brown sugar with an electric mixer in a large bowl until smooth. Beat in one egg until completely incorporated. Beat in the last egg along with the vanilla. Mix in the flour mixture until just incorporated. Fold in the chocolate chips; mixing just enough to evenly combine. Drop by heaped teaspoonfuls onto ungreased baking sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until the edges are golden, 9 to 12 minutes. Allow the cookies to cool on the baking sheet for 1 minute before removing to a wire rack to cool completely.

review.reviewBody: These were yummy and VERY chocolatey...to the person who said they came out flat...it is CRUCIAL that you thoroughly mix any cookie recipe ingredients. Can't stress that enough. You can sift the dry ingredients to be sure those get mixed well and then USE A HAND MIXER when you add in the wet ingredients prior to adding the chips. Don't use the mixer when you add the chips. The cookies should be puffy when they come out of the oven and then flatten as they cool.

Delicious! I made it with Ener-G Egg replacer and Blue Bonnet Light because of food allergies. They turned out perfectly. The dough was so sticky I thought for sure they would turn out super flat, but they were seriously perfect. I didn't really pay that much attention to mixing the dry first and then the wet. I used a kitchen-aid mixer which may be why it didn't matter. I did cream the butter and sugar first, then I added the Ener-G Egg Replacer, baking soda, and vanilla. Then I added the rest of the dry ingredients. We used Enjoy Life chocolate chips. If you underbake them a bit they taste like brownies. They are really good completely baked too. ETA: In my non-convection oven if I bake for 12 mins they are still a little underbaked. I have to cook for 14-15 minutes for them to be fully cooked.

Love this recipe! I read the comments and liked the one about adding mint extract to make it taste like a Girl Scout Thin Mint. I added 1 tsp spearmint extract and used Nestle Dark Chocolate and Mint Morsels, for a double shot of mint flavor. I baked some as drop cookies and some in a mini-muffin tin. I will make this again.

Really good. I added 1 cup of chopped macadamias and a dash of salt. Also an extra half tsp. Vanilla. Perfect consistency. Soft yet slightly chewy. 3" dia cookies took 10 min in my oven, on heavy duty stainless cookie sheets, one sheet at a time.

Wonderful. I just added 1/2 tsp salt and only 1/3 cup cocoa powder. I was afraid it would be a little too rich with all of it. I also used 1/3 cup canola oil abd 1/2 cup butter instead of 1 cup of butter...like I do in all my recipes. My husband prefers the consistency that this creates better. They are a little softer and puffier. I also only cook them for 7 minutes at 375 degrees. But over all, they were delicious!!

Amazing cookie recipe. I followed exactly and baked at 10 minutes. All came out perfect. I like a flater cookie, so I rolled dough in to 1 teaspoon balls and pressed down with a fork before baking. Topped with some melted chocolate chips and crushed peppermint for a Christmas cookie swap. Thank you !

Split batter in thirds:

Yum!

These cookies were a huge hit with my young adult kids. The flavor is great. They didn't last long. One thing I'd like to improve is that they were under done. I think it's because I made them too large, so next time, I would drop smaller scoops onto cookie sheet before baking. It would also help probably if I chilled the dough prior to scooping, but I usually don't plan that far ahead. I'll definitely make these again.

Made a batch of these chocolate delights, adding about 1 1/2 cups of chopped walnuts, and they were so fabulous, I immediately made a second batch to take to work to share, where they were also a huge hit! These are a recipe to KEEP. Chocolate is full flavored and crisp and crunchy. And they are delightfully gooey and soft on the inside while still warm!

Chocolate lovers dream! My husband loved these. I used unsweetened applesauce for the butter, cut both sugars to 1/4 c each, 1 1/2 c a/p flour and 1/2 c white wheat flour, and also added 1/2 tsp of salt. They came out light and fluffy, a keeper recipe!

Soooooo yummy! I used the back of a spoon to make a small indent in them and filled it with peanut butter frosting.

Also added 1/2 t salt like some other reviews called for.

I used 60% cacao chocolate chips and I guess just regular cocoa powder, not dark chocolate. They were very chocolatey, almost to the point they were a tad bit bitter. So if you don't want the bitter, don't use dark chocolate chips. But the more cacao they have, the healthier they are. Nothing wrong with trying to make your dessert more healthy, is there? You decide.
I enjoyed this recipe, i added a 1/2 teaspoon if salt; and it turned out great. It had great spinability. Turns out green food coloring doesn't show up well in it though.
I added chopped walnuts. They were the life of the party!
These cookies are absolutely gorgeous! I didn't add chocolate chips nor vanila, but they turned out amazing!! 100% recommend making!

These cookies were soooo good and ez to make. My husband loved them and I would definitely make again.
Super easy and yummy. I’m not a fan of chocolate but these could change my mind.
